arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Texas argues the River Master's decision causes incalculable economic harm. Texas claims this harm occurs if New Mexico redeems credits during a drought.
New Mexico argues Texas explicitly requested the water storage. New Mexico states this request justifies charging Texas for the resulting evaporative losses.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned the relevance of forfeiture and waiver doctrines. He suggested the Court would not decide this case on those grounds.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The River Master awarded New Mexico a credit for evaporative losses. Texas argues this credit wrongly shifts the cost to its farmers. New Mexico argues Texas requested the storage and should pay for the loss.

New Mexico wants the Court to uphold the evaporative loss credit. New Mexico argues Texas requested the storage and should bear the cost.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Texas argues the River Master erred in applying the manual section for requested storage. Texas claims this decision deprives west Texas of a year's irrigation water.
New Mexico argues Texas made an express request for storage. New Mexico contends this request triggers the manual provision that charges the requesting state for losses.

paragraphs: This dispute determines which state pays for water lost to evaporation. The outcome affects irrigation water availability for farmers in west Texas. It also impacts economic stability for businesses relying on that water supply.
